endorsements.quote: Establishing interdisciplinary governance structures—such as clinical AI committees or ethics boards—can help ensure that AI tools remain aligned with both patient safety and institutional values.
Engaging stakeholders in the process is vital, as well as considering their inputs on needs, daily struggles, and feedback.
After deployment, designated health care staff and engineers or data scientists must track outcomes, monitor changes, and ensure tool efficiency in this high-stakes setting.
On a larger scale, a multidisciplinary team could periodically review dashboards and scorecards to measure the efficacy of the deployed tool.

Use large data sets that represent all demographics before developing and training AI models to avoid biased outputs and recommendations 58 Ensuring transparency in AI decision-making Requiring explainable AI outputs and documentation to build clinician trust and meet regulatory standards 90 Pilot testing and monitoring outcomes PDSA cycles can be used to test changes and measure the outcomes of those changes.

If no training is given to the next class of medical trainees, they may not trust the tool and/or misinterpret the signals, resulting in missed early interventions and potentially causing preventable harm.
During the sustain phase, a plan should be put in place that involves continuously ensuring data security and privacy through robust encryption, informed consent, and audit trails.
A good tool for reporting standards is the Minimum Information for Medical AI Reporting (MINIMAR), which develops reporting standards for AI in health care.

Developers, engineers, and health care leaders must understand regulatory frameworks, such as the International Medical Device Regulators Forum, the software as a Medical Device Guidelines from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the General Data Protection Regulations from the European Union.

unlisted_practices: Perform process improvement and workflow redesign before deploying AI or automation.
Apply plan-do-study-act improvement cycles to test and refine AI tools before clinical release.
Establish standard operating procedures and standard work documentation to sustain AI performance gains.
Use process simulation or digital twins to predict intervention impact before full-scale deployment.
Harmonize data formats, performance metrics, and communication protocols, using interoperability standards such as FHIR, to scale AI across organizations.
Share outcome results openly, including cases where AI caused harm or noise, and report negative outcomes.
Use external validation to identify flaws in AI systems and evaluate patient safety.
Routinely review and validate AI data labeling, analysis, and reporting in a transparent manner to mitigate bias.

screen.reason: Presents the Understand-Transform-Sustain (UTS) quality improvement and governance framework for AI deployment in health care, without an empirical study testing outcomes.
